PERFECT DAYS

Trailer
Directed by Wim Wenders
Japan, Germany, 2023
Drama
  • 125125 minutes

Synopsis

Hirayama lives a life of blissful contentment, spending his days balancing his job as a caretaker of Tokyo’s public toilets with his passion for music, literature, and photography. His structured routine is slowly interrupted by unexpected encounters that force him to reconnect with his past.

MORE LIKE THIS

  • Ruminating on life and architecture in the eponymous Indiana city, this meditative drama is the feature debut from writer-director Kogonada (After Yang). As soulful as it is conceptually rigorous, Columbus vitally reinvigorates the emotional and intellectual awakenings of the coming-of-age genre.

    COLUMBUS

    Kogonada United States 2017

  • The first Singaporean to have his films invited to major festivals—Toronto, Berlin and Cannes among others— Eric Khoo is the man behind this food-themed drama about the act of discovering your family roots. At once gentle and straightforward, Ramen Shop will undeniably work up an appetite.

    RAMEN SHOP

    Eric Khoo Singapore 2018

  • A dazzlingly moving tale of chance and romance in Mumbai, The Lunchbox was a worldwide success, and one of the Indian hits of the recent decades. A gentle and charming portrait of loneliness and disenchantment within the huge, modern city, where two souls cross paths through a most uncommon manner.

    THE LUNCHBOX

    Ritesh Batra India 2013

  • Everyday dreamers imagine their attachments scattering to the breeze and becoming someone else in these tableaux of summertime Berlin. As Angela Schanelec threads serendipities—music, movement, tenderness—into ennui’s enervating haze, she outlines the pattern for her critically acclaimed cinema.

    PASSING SUMMER

    Angela Schanelec Germany 2001

  • Influenced by Italian neorealism, Wadjda is a heartfelt and charming tale about a child’s conviction against the odds. Both the first woman director from Saudi Arabia, and the first filmmaker to entirely shoot a film there, Haifaa Al-Mansour crafts this delightful hymn to the heft of small battles.

    WADJDA

    Haifaa Al-Mansour Saudi Arabia 2012

  • Joanna Hogg, one of Britain’s best directors, transitioned with this film from working in television to a new, completely unpredictable career in cinema. A penetrating and carefully balanced examination of the class that can vacation in Italy, starring Tom Hiddleston.

    UNRELATED

    Joanna Hogg United Kingdom 2007

  • Plugging into the all-consuming headspace of teenagedom, this beloved cult film rings with the catchy euphoria of a well-penned rock chorus. A hangout movie shaped by moments of sublime intensity and loose stretches of lazy downtime, Linda Linda Linda lives in the endless present of youth.

    LINDA LINDA LINDA

    Nobuhiro Yamashita Japan 2005

  • For his 1969 feature debut, director Alain Tanner (In the White City) transplants the revolutionary spark and spirit of May ‘68 to his native Switzerland, intelligently examining a man’s attempt to trade his comfortable bourgeois life for the counterculture. Winner of Locarno’s Golden Leopard!

    CHARLES, DEAD OR ALIVE

    Alain Tanner Switzerland 1969

  • A whirlwind mix of DV tapes and 16mm stock, Haley Elizabeth Anderson’s singular debut transforms the concrete jungle of New York into a delicate tapestry of emotions. Charting the four seasons of a magnetic young woman unsettled by change, Tendaberry composes an urban symphony in the key of love.

    TENDABERRY

    Haley Elizabeth Anderson United States 2024

  • Quick cash proves to be more than just a pipe dream in Bill Forsyth’s buoyant debut about a group of Glaswegian lads who speculate to accumulate in ludicrous fashion. Shrugging off a gloomy tradition of kitchen-sink realism, this cheery comedy looks at the follies of youth with genuine affection.

    THAT SINKING FEELING

    Bill Forsyth United Kingdom 1979

  • Argentine director Gonzalo Castro manages to capture the beauty of everyday life in this experimental portrait of the one-armed Mexican novelist (and ultimate prankster!) Mario Bellatín. Just like Bellatín’s fiction, the film treads a fine line between “truth” and “fiction”—wait, is the joke on us?

    WINTER HOUSE

    Gonzalo Castro Argentina 2010

  • Irène Jacob won Best Actress in Cannes for her magnificent dual roles in this lyrical masterwork from Polish auteur Krzysztof Kieślowski. With its luminous cinematography and unforgettable score, The Double Life of Véronique is a magical and enigmatic tale of love, ambition, and twinned identities.

    THE DOUBLE LIFE OF VÉRONIQUE

    Krzysztof Kieślowski France 1991
